newsitem.title: USA: Calif. panel backs $20-bln-plus speed rail plan.
newsitem.headline: Calif. panel backs $20-bln-plus speed rail plan.

text.p: A California state commission approved its final report on Friday calling on the state to develop and operate a multi-billion dollar high speed rail system that would link its major cities.

Capital costs to build the massive rail system are an estimated $20.7 billion to $28.9 billion, depending on the type of rail system used, according to the Intercity High Speed Rail Commission, which backed the $20.7 billion design.
To help pay for the massive project, bonds would likely be sold backed by either gasoline or sales tax revenues, Daniel Leavitt, executive director of the commission, said.

The commission said a 1/4-cent statewide sales tax and a 6-cent gas tax were the best financing options for the rail system, which would link San Francisco to Los Angeles, Los Angeles to San Diego, and Stockton to Sacramento.

"This is something that the people can get behind, that is good for the state," Leavitt said after the commission, meeting in San Francisco, approved its final report, submitting it to the governor and the Legislature for review.
By reducing congestion on other modes, high speed rail could save California taxpayers over $1 billion annually in delay costs and other savings, the panel said in its report.
Responsibility for implementing the report's recommendations will fall to a new High Speed Rail Authority, created by legislation signed by Gov. Pete Wilson this year.
The measure authorized the new High Speed Rail Authority to submit a project and financing plan for a high speed rail train network in the state to the voters for approval by the year 2000.
